one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent incorrectly concluded that regex-based chess move generation is computationally impossible, drifted into irrelevant exploit-style probes and non-general hardcoded regexes, created a fake artifact (chess_move_generator.py) that cannot be invoked by the harness, and ultimately abandoned the task explicitly despite a feasible reference solution existing.
t_err_evidence: Step 3: Agent frames the problem as 'an impossible task' and 'practically impossible' in the analysis, forming the false premise that drives all subsequent misdirected behavior. It then begins a futile system-wide filesystem scan rather than attempting a valid regex construction strategy.
t_commit_evidence: Step 13: Agent explicitly declares 'Unable to create a working solution' and prints an abandonment message, locking in failure by halting all implementation attempts before producing any valid re.json.
t_surface_evidence: Step 13: The agent echoes 'Unable to create a working solution: Implementing a full chess move generator using regex patterns is computationally impossible...' — the first observable failure signal visible in terminal output.
trigger_explanation: At step 3, the agent acts on the unverified assumption that implementing chess move generation with regex patterns is fundamentally impossible. This belief is false — a reference solution exists — but the agent never challenges it, causing all subsequent effort to be misdirected toward workarounds (subprocess calls, external scripts) or hardcoded position-specific hacks rather than genuine regex-based move generation.
forewarning_evidence: Step 8: The agent writes a Python script importing the chess module, despite having confirmed in step 4 that 'chess module not available'. The script then fails with ModuleNotFoundError — a clear disconfirming signal the agent had already seen but ignored.
fabrication_evidence: Step 10: Agent creates /app/chess_move_generator.py using the chess library (unavailable in environment) and marks it executable, as if it will be invoked by the harness — which only reads /app/re.json string replacements and never calls external scripts. Step 11: Agent writes re.json with a replacement string containing embedded Python subprocess code, presenting it as a functioning solution when re.sub only applies string substitution and will not execute the code.
